feed.title: Combined summary - [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay

entry.title: Combined summary - [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
entry.summary: The `staletip` proposal is an innovative approach designed to improve the observability of stale rates within the Bitcoin network, which are indicative of the network's health and can reveal issues related to block propagation delays. This system operates on a peer-to-peer basis, allowing nodes that opt-in to communicate information about detected stale tips to each other. The initiative builds upon prior work by AJ Towns and has been further developed through the collaborative efforts of pseudoramdom and w0xlt, who have also provided a draft of the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) and a proof-of-concept for practical examination ([Draft BIP](https://github.com/pseudoramdom/bips/blob/staletip-bip-draft/bip-staletip.md), [Proof-of-concept](https://github.com/w0xlt/bitcoin/tree/staletip-v4)). Stale blocks occur when two valid blocks are discovered nearly simultaneously at the same chain height, creating challenges in monitoring and understanding their origins due to existing technologies like compact block relay and FIBRE, which focus on rapidly propagating the longest chain. These technologies often result in stale branches going unnoticed unless they are actively monitored, and even then, only parts of the branches may be visible. High stale rates could indicate significant underlying issues such as network partitions or adversarial mining strategies, thus making tools like `staletip` essential for better diagnostics and quicker reorganization handling. The technical specifications of `staletip` involve using BIP 434 `feature` messages for nodes to signal their support for this function. Communication is limited to tips within 1000 blocks of the active chain tip to prevent sharing outdated or irrelevant data, and header sequences are restricted to 20 compressed headers to control the scope of information shared. Each node maintains a cache of up to 10 recent tips to ensure efficient data transmission without overburdening the network. By implementing `staletip`, developers aim to equip nodes with improved information on network events, potentially leading to faster response times during active branch switches and deeper insights into block propagation dynamics and stale rate occurrences. Feedback on the implementation of `staletip` has highlighted some potential concerns, particularly regarding how it might affect the broader purpose of the network. There are apprehensions about the new system introducing additional vulnerabilities to denial-of-service (DoS) attacks and enabling fingerprinting vectors. However, the design includes several protective measures to mitigate these risks, such as bounded processing by branch length, recency, and retained-tip limits, and options for nodes to disable the feature if the trade-offs are deemed unacceptable. Moreover, the protocol handles scenarios with more than one competing chain by announcing competing branches in separate messages, thus maintaining clarity and efficiency in communication. The ongoing documentation efforts for mainnet stale blocks, which require continuous monitoring of several long-running nodes, underscore the relevance and potential utility of the `staletip` proposal from both monitoring and research perspectives ([ongoing documentation effort](https://github.com/bitcoin-data/stale-blocks)).
